name: MonarchStackedProportionBar
title: StackedProportionBar
wrapsNative: GeometryReader with an HStack of Rectangle segments clipped to a Capsule; MonarchChartLegend (square markers) as the legend, or a MonarchFlowLayout list for status tones and the remainder
summary: One horizontal bar split into proportions, with a legend that lists each part's value and share.
whenToUse: To show how one whole divides (pipeline stages, storage by type, monitors by state) inside a card or row where a donut chart would be too large. With total and remainderLabel it shows the use of a capacity.
whenNotToUse: For one value against a target, use ProgressView with .monarch or MonarchUsageMeter. To rank or compare many parts, use MonarchBarList. For breakdowns over time, use a stacked bar chart.
api: MonarchStackedProportionBar.init(_ label: String, segments: [MonarchStackedProportionBarSegment], total: Double? = nil, remainderLabel: String? = nil, legendContent: MonarchStackedProportionBarLegendContent = .both, size: MonarchStackedProportionBarSize = .md, showsLegend: Bool = true, hidesZero: Bool = true, percentDigits: Int = 0, emptyLabel: String? = nil, formatValue: ((Double) -> String)? = nil)
MonarchStackedProportionBarSegment.init(_ key: String, label: String, value: Double, color: MonarchChartColor? = nil)
MonarchStackedProportionBarSegment.init(_ key: String, label: String, value: Double, tone: MonarchTone)
enum MonarchStackedProportionBarSize { case sm, md, lg }
enum MonarchStackedProportionBarLegendContent { case both, value, percent, none }

options.name: label
options.description: Names the legend for VoiceOver, such as "Lead pipeline".

options.name: segments
options.description: The parts, in display order. Each has a key, a label, a value, and a palette colour or a status tone.

options.name: total
options.description: The size of the whole, for a capacity. The sum of the parts when nil or smaller than the sum; the rest is empty track.

options.name: remainderLabel
options.description: The legend name of the empty remainder, such as "Free". Without it the remainder is drawn but not listed.

options.name: legendContent
options.description: What each legend entry shows after its label: both ("1,204 · 34%"), value, percent or none.

options.name: size
options.description: The thickness of the bar: sm 4, md 8 or lg 12 points.

options.name: showsLegend
options.description: Whether the legend is drawn. Off, VoiceOver still reads every entry from the bar.

options.name: hidesZero
options.description: Whether parts with a value of 0 are left out of the bar and the legend.

options.name: percentDigits
options.description: The decimal places of shares. Shares too small to write read "<1%".

options.name: emptyLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in text "No data yet", shown when every value is 0.

options.name: formatValue
options.description: Writes a value. The default is a number in the environment's locale.

states.name: default
states.description: The parts in palette colours, in order, each at least 4 points wide, separated by 2-point gaps; the legend lists every part.

states.name: status mode
states.description: Every segment has a tone: segments and legend markers use the solid tone colours, and neutral uses the subtle text colour.

states.name: remainder
states.description: A total above the sum leaves empty track; with remainderLabel it is listed with an outlined marker.

states.name: legend hidden
states.description: Only the bar is drawn; VoiceOver reads the label and every entry.

states.name: empty
states.description: Every value is 0 or there are no segments: an empty track and "No data yet".

appearance: Segments use the theme's data colours 1 to 5 in order (the sixth part and later are neutral), or in status mode the solid success, warning, danger and info colours and the subtle text colour. The track is the muted background. The legend is caption text in the default text colour. The same roles are used in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web shows a native tooltip when the pointer hovers a segment; touch has no hover, so the legend carries every value and there is no tooltip. The web minSegmentWidth option is a fixed 4 points here. The web locale and valueFormat options are the environment locale and formatValue. A mix of tones and palette colours is not rejected by the type system as on the web; tones are ignored, as the web does at run time. Segments are laid out from the leading edge, so the bar is mirrored in right-to-left layouts. Android uses the same names.
accessibility: The bar is hidden from VoiceOver while the legend is shown; the legend is a container named by label.
Each legend entry is one element read as its label, then its value and share, such as "Replied, 182 · 9%".
With showsLegend off, the bar is one element read as label with every entry as its value.
With no data, one element reads the label and "No data yet".
Every part has a text label, so no part is told apart by colour alone; the remainder's marker is outlined, not filled.
Legend text scales with Dynamic Type and wraps onto more rows.
edgeCases: Negative and non-finite values count as 0.
A share under 1% reads "<1%" and one just under the whole reads ">99%" (with percentDigits, the thresholds move by the same number of places).
Many tiny parts can need more than the bar's width at their minimum; the excess is clipped by the capsule.
Palette slots follow the segment's position before zeros are hidden, so hiding a zero part never repaints the others. Pin color when a filter can remove parts.
A total smaller than the sum is ignored.
Status mode needs a tone on every segment; a partial set of tones is ignored.

examples.title: Pipeline stages
examples.template:
MonarchStackedProportionBar(
    {{label}},
    segments: [
        MonarchStackedProportionBarSegment({{segments.0.key}}, label: {{segments.0.label}}, value: {{segments.0.value}}),
        MonarchStackedProportionBarSegment({{segments.1.key}}, label: {{segments.1.label}}, value: {{segments.1.value}}),
        MonarchStackedProportionBarSegment({{segments.2.key}}, label: {{segments.2.label}}, value: {{segments.2.value}}),
        MonarchStackedProportionBarSegment({{segments.3.key}}, label: {{segments.3.label}}, value: {{segments.3.value}}),
        MonarchStackedProportionBarSegment({{segments.4.key}}, label: {{segments.4.label}}, value: {{segments.4.value}}),
    ]
)
.frame(maxWidth: 512)
.environment(\.locale, Locale(identifier: {{locale}}))
examples.code:
MonarchStackedProportionBar(
    "Lead pipeline",
    segments: [
        MonarchStackedProportionBarSegment("new", label: "New", value: 1240),
        MonarchStackedProportionBarSegment("enrolled", label: "In a campaign", value: 610),
        MonarchStackedProportionBarSegment("replied", label: "Replied", value: 182),
        MonarchStackedProportionBarSegment("converted", label: "Converted", value: 41),
        MonarchStackedProportionBarSegment("unsubscribed", label: "Unsubscribed", value: 6),
    ]
)
.frame(maxWidth: 512)
.environment(\.locale, Locale(identifier: "en-US"))

examples.title: Storage capacity with a remainder
examples.code:
MonarchStackedProportionBar(
    "Storage",
    segments: [
        MonarchStackedProportionBarSegment("media", label: "Media", value: 42),
        MonarchStackedProportionBarSegment("docs", label: "Documents", value: 18),
    ],
    total: 100,
    remainderLabel: "Free",
    legendContent: .value,
    size: .lg,
    formatValue: { "\(Int($0)) GB" }
)

examples.title: Monitors by state
examples.code:
MonarchStackedProportionBar(
    "Monitors",
    segments: [
        MonarchStackedProportionBarSegment("up", label: "Operational", value: 41, tone: .success),
        MonarchStackedProportionBarSegment("slow", label: "Degraded", value: 3, tone: .warning),
        MonarchStackedProportionBarSegment("down", label: "Down", value: 1, tone: .danger),
    ],
    size: .sm
)
